narrative.overview:
Stockball combines the compressed information rhythm of a live market board with the atmosphere of a floodlit football ground. It is dark, focused, and data-forward: charcoal layers hold dense player information while a restrained steel-blue accent makes navigation and action states immediately legible.

The interface should feel technical without becoming specialist-only. Orbitron gives the market-discovery experience one unmistakable football-tech voice, including its headline values. IBM Plex Mono is reserved for dense portfolio analysis and technical shortcuts. Production surfaces are compact but not cramped, with clear section framing, repeated row structures, and plain-language context around market data.
keyCharacteristics: Dark charcoal canvas with subtly stepped panels and cool borders.
Steel-blue accent used selectively for actions, focus, and active navigation.
Orbitron across the main interface and homepage market data; IBM Plex Mono only for dense portfolio analysis and technical shortcuts.
Dense, repeatable market rows with strong alignment and restrained status color.
Explicit virtual-market language wherever account balances or player prices appear.

rules.name: The Incumbent Palette Rule
rules.body: Only the charcoal, steel-blue, green, and red production palette documented here is approved. New palette experiments require a separate explicit design decision before promotion into product work.

rules.name: The Signal, Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Blue, green, and red communicate action, selection, focus, or market direction; they are not ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Orbitron owns the interface and the market-discovery experience, including visible prices and changes. IBM Plex Mono is limited to dense portfolio analysis and technical shortcuts. Do not introduce a third production family.

rules.name: The Numbers Line Up Rule
rules.body: Numeric market content uses tabular numerals and a slashed zero so repeated values remain easy to compare.

rules.name: The Alternating Movers Rule
rules.body: Keep gainers and decliners in one DOM-ordered feed: gainer one, decliner one, gainer two, decliner two. Direction remains explicit through the signed percentage and an accessible rank description, never colour alone.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Do not add ambient card shadows. Establish hierarchy with surface tone, borders, and state-specific fills.

dos: Do use Orbitron as the default face for headings, body copy, labels, navigation, controls, and player names.
Do use Orbitron for homepage prices, percentages, ranks, and times; reserve IBM Plex Mono for dense portfolio tables and keyboard shortcuts.
Do preserve the charcoal/steel-blue production palette and use green/red only for directional market state.
Do keep virtual-market and live-data disclosures legible near relevant balances and prices.
Do preserve keyboard focus visibility, reduced-motion behavior, and horizontal scrolling for dense comparisons.
Do pair pointer chart inspection with a labeled keyboard-operable range input and announce the inspected price and timestamp politely.
Do preserve metric labels, percentile ordinals, and raw values when the radar becomes a mobile list.
Do keep football percentiles position-relative and state that trading activity—not football statistics—determines price.
donts: Don't introduce an alternate palette without first documenting its role and contrast behavior.
Don't use Oxanium, Rajdhani, or Chakra Petch in production without a new explicit typography decision.
Don't add ambient shadows, decorative gradients, or broad accent fills that weaken the data hierarchy.
Don't let IBM Plex Mono dominate the market homepage or use it as the general interface face.
Don't imply real-money investing through copy, imagery, or component treatment.
Don't shrink a radar chart until its labels become illegible; switch to the divided metric list below 640px.
Don't communicate chart direction or profile performance through colour or geometry alone.
